prize_parts.citation: for introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory and showing how reallocation across firms shapes the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: B048, with Melitz and Helpman as the only credited names. The discovery is a mechanism. Firms differ in productivity, only the more productive ones select into exporting, and liberalisation reallocates resources toward them, which creates a distinct channel for the gains from trade. Melitz (2003) is the originating model. Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, together with his earlier trade theory, makes him the natural second name. The qualitative predictions (exporter premia, selection into exporting, within-industry reallocation) have been tested in firm-level data across many countries for over twenty years. The idea has also spread into macro, growth and development, where reallocation and misallocation are standard concepts. I read the round-1 exchange as showing that the real contest is between B048 and B001, and that it turns on what has survived testing and on how cleanly credit can be assigned within a three-name cap. On both, B048 looks stronger to me. Its core predictions are tested, and its two-name credit carries the central model and its main extension. B001's central causal claim is contested, and the cap forces out Vishny, a co-author of the founding papers. The 2008 prize covered earlier new trade theory with representative firms, so this is a distinct advance. I do not count the opening-ranking tallies or the number of round-1 supporters as evidence of merit.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is priority. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum developed closely parallel firm-level facts and models, and they are not on this ballot entry. A Melitz-Helpman credit could therefore be read as under-crediting the empirical foundations. I agree with Hjalmarsson that this is a real vulnerability and not only a drafting issue, and the three-name cap cannot resolve it. Some welfare magnitudes also depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity, so the discovery should be framed as the qualitative mechanism and not as a measured size of the gains. Helpman also appears in another candidate package (B026), which complicates the framing of his credit. Trade was recognised in 2008. I count that as a field-balance consideration and not as evidence about merit.

responses.point: Friberg keeps B001 first with moderate confidence. He concedes it does not compete on identification strength and rests the case on field creation: new cross-country data on investor protection and ownership, a clear framing, and decades of replication and critique. He treats B048 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I appreciate his candour about identification. I take his point that the critiques are part of what maturity means, and that the data and the question the programme made central do not depend on every causal claim surviving. If the citation rested only on that, B001 would be a coherent prize. Even so, two costs remain for me. Vishny's exclusion changes who is credited for the founding papers, and the legal-origins reading is the part a citation would find hardest to avoid implying. B048's core predictions have been tested directly against firm-level data, and its credit divides cleanly between two names. I therefore keep B001 as my first alternative and not my preferred part.

responses.point: Hassler, the chair, prefers B001 and would word the citation around measurable institutions and the investor-protection research programme, not around legal origin as a proven cause. He values the creation of a new field somewhat more than refinement within an established one, calls the gap with B048 small, and says he would take B048 seriously.
responses.response: I agree that wording the citation around measurable institutions and established regularities is the best version of B001, and I would not oppose it as a fallback. My difference is on weighting. I do not think B048 is mere refinement within an established field. It replaced the representative-firm unit of analysis and added a new welfare channel, and it did so with a mechanism that has been tested. A citation that avoids the causal claim also gives up the explanatory content that would make B001 a discovery and not a data resource. I note that Hassler discloses his role as chair and his B001 preference, and that he is my IIES colleague. I treat that as disclosed and do not adjudicate it.

responses.point: Krusell, the secretary, prefers B037 (Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler) and disagrees with my seventh-place opening rank. He argues that the 2022 prize addressed banking and the origins of crises, whereas Kiyotaki-Moore concerns amplification through collateral values, so the overlap is a reduction in marginal novelty and not a bar.
responses.response: I accept the distinction and the correction. The overlap with the 2022 prize is not disqualifying, and Kiyotaki and Moore are a clean, mature core. My seventh-place opening rank did weigh that overlap too heavily. I still do not put B037 first, for two reasons. Empirical identification of collateral channels is weaker than the theory's influence suggests, and the credit for a third name (Gertler) is split with B040 and with Bernanke's earlier recognition. Krusell himself says a two-name prize is the fallback. B037 is a defensible outcome, but I do not rank it above B048 on the discovery and attribution criteria. It is not among my named alternatives, because B001 and B015 are the closer contests in my judgement. Krusell and I are frequent co-authors, which I disclose and do not adjudicate.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers B048 and calls the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line the real vulnerability, because it concerns priority on the empirical foundations and not only a later extension. She would draft the citation around the selection mechanism and gains-from-trade framework so that it does not overclaim the empirical firm-level facts.
responses.response: I agree with her, and this answers the chair's first question for B048 supporters. A citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism does not remove the priority concern, but it keeps the prize from claiming the empirical foundations. That is why my wording speaks of introducing selection into trade theory and showing how reallocation shapes the gains. It makes no claim about who first documented firm-level trade facts. If the committee judged that the priority question was material and could not be handled by wording, I would reconsider and look first at B001 on a data-and-design citation. I do not judge it material at present, because the model and its main extension are what carry the selection mechanism.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum priority question as material, which this ballot entry and the three-name cap cannot accommodate.
How Helpman's separate appearance in B026 affects the framing and support for his credit here. I would define the B048 citation tightly around the selection discovery.
How much the welfare-gain magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions, and whether that weakens the claim to a robust discovery. I think it does not for the qualitative mechanism.
Whether B001 should rank above B048 if the committee accepts a citation resting only on the data and research design and judges the identification critiques less damaging than I do.
Whether thematic overlap with recent prizes should count as evidence about novelty at the margin, or only as timing. I treat the 2008 trade prize and field rotation as not bearing on merit.
My assessments rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Melitz, Helpman, Shleifer, La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn is documented in my supplied profile. I disclose a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow (credited on B007, which is not in my configuration or alternatives). I am a frequent co-author of Per Krusell (secretary, B037 supporter) and a co-author of John Hassler (chair, B001 supporter), and I am an IIES colleague of both. I also disclose that my own research on reallocation, misallocation and creative destruction is adjacent to the B048 mechanism, so I may be biased toward it. I have tried to apply the same criteria to all candidates. My profile suggests I may have helped draft Academy background material on a recent prize, which has no apparent bearing on these candidates. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
